purpose: Lindane is used to treat scabies (a skin infestation caused by tiny mites) and lice, including head lice and pubic lice. It is typically used when other safer treatments have not worked. It kills the parasites living on your skin or scalp.
how_it_works: Lindane works by being absorbed into the nervous system of the lice or mites, overstimulating their nerves and causing them to die. Think of it like a poison that targets the bugs but is applied to your skin. Because it can also affect the human nervous system, it must be used very carefully and only as directed.
common_side_effects: Some people may notice skin irritation, redness, itching, or a burning or tingling sensation where the lotion or shampoo was applied. These are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Lindane is a second-line treatment and should only be used if other options have failed, because it can be absorbed through the skin and may cause serious nervous system side effects, including seizures. It should NOT be used in infants, young children, pregnant or breastfeeding women, elderly patients, or people with seizure disorders. Never use more than prescribed, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Keep it away from your eyes and mouth.
typical_dosing: For scabies, a thin layer of lindane lotion is applied to dry skin from the neck down, left on for 8 to 12 hours, then thoroughly washed off — usually just one application. For lice, the shampoo is worked into the affected hair, left on for only 4 minutes, then rinsed out completely. Do not reapply unless your doctor specifically tells you to.
